messages:
mae: noticed a few  tail latency blips this morning on the dedupe job after that runtime kernel selector change. traces show kernel pick flip mid-request and KV cache churn.
arjun: saw the same in prod-canary. looks like hw detect is returning later than before so the initial request takes the wrong fastpath.
lucy: wait we probe on startup right? why would it be late?
mae: we do, but when pods are restored (k8s preempt/evict) the in-memory hw signature cache is lost. runtime re-probes lazily on first inference and sometimes the probe happens after the first batch has already chosen a kernel. that first batch gets the wrong execution path.
toni: that matches the profiler output I pulled. kv-cache gets evicted and batching heuristics mis-align. can you paste the profiler snippet?
mae: here's the small log excerpt from the pod that hit 58ms on a single request (normal ~12ms):
```
[2026-03-07T09:14:02.123Z] probe_hw: deferred -> result: sm=86, tensor_cores=1, bf16=1, fp8=0
[2026-03-07T09:14:02.124Z] pick_kernel: fastpath_seq32 (chosen based on initial seqlen bucket)
[2026-03-07T09:14:02.184Z] reconfigure: detected seq>64, switching to generic_seq128; kv-cache flush triggered
[2026-03-07T09:14:02.186Z] execute_kernel: generic_seq128 latency=58ms
```
arjun: looks like the decision tree uses (seqlen bucket + sm_flags) and the late probe causes a reconfigure that flushes KV and resets batching.
lucy: possible mitigations: 1) eagerly probe on container start, 2) persist hw fingerprint to local disk so restarts read it back, 3) make kernel decision idempotent so a late probe doesn't force an expensive reconfigure mid-request.
toni: also double-check the tensor-core / bf16 handshake. some driver combinations report bf16 support but tensor cores are effectively disabled under certain compute modes; that mismatch yields big perf deltas without an obvious error.
mae: repro steps I used: run a cold pod, trigger a single long request to force seqlen>128 on first inference and capture `/var/log/runtime/prof.log`. repro command: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- /usr/local/bin/runtime --probe-on-demand --rt-prof --dump` and then send a seq128 payload. gist with full steps (internal): https://redwood-internal/repro/3632 (placeholder).
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for runtime v2.14.2 to cluster-a (10 pods)
arjun: proposal: add a startup-probe that runs before healthcheck returns (3 quick probes with backoff) + persist hw sig to `/var/lib/runtime/hwsig` and read it on restart. if probe flips repeatedly mark node as unstable and put it on a short blacklist. also add a small runtime guard: if first-token latency > 30ms route that request to a higher-latency-safe variant (fallback model) to avoid user-visible tail spikes.
lucy: sounds good. I'll draft the PR for the startup-probe flag and the hwsig persistence (will add unit tests for read/write and a k8s init check).
toni: I'll run end-to-end perf matrix for seq32/64/128/256 with and without tensor-core enabled and upload `rt-prof --dump` artifacts to the perf bucket.
mae: marking this P0 perf regression for oncall. adding checklist: 1) startup probe PR 2) persist hwsig 3) add metric for probe-late events 4) add node-blacklist logic 5) end-to-end perf tests.
mae: thanks everyone, will follow up in the PR comments.
